coordinates: Team-relative feet: fx is distance up ice from the team's own goal line (0 = own goal line, 64 = own blue line, 89 = center red line, 114 = far blue line, 178 = far goal line); fy is across the ice, 0 to 85, 42.5 = center. Each formation lists a spot per role (LW, C, RW, LD, RD); null means that role is the pressurer and chases the carrier.

boards.label: Up the boards
boards.desc: D behind the net, wingers on the half walls, center swings through the middle.

stretch.label: Stretch pass
stretch.desc: Wingers fly to the far blue line for a long pass; vulnerable to the trap and to icing.

reverse.label: Reverse (D to D)
reverse.desc: D-to-D behind the net to change the point of attack.

flow.desc: Breakout timing. Once the team has had the puck for startAfterSec the forwards leave their support spots and burst north, settling ahead of the puck by their ahead distance (capped at maxFx so nobody is offside early) over rampSec. The carrier skates it out with speed instead of cruising.

neutralAttack.desc: Weak-side winger is the lead forward riding the far blue line (max fx 108); strong-side winger drives the boards (puck fx + 14); center drives the middle lane as the trailer (puck fx + 4); D trail by 18.

headman.label: Headman to lead F
headman.desc: Move the puck to the lead forward whenever the lane is there.

carry.label: Carry, drive wide
carry.desc: Carry in wide; pass only under pressure.

chip.label: Chip and chase
chip.desc: Chip the puck past a defender standing up at the line and chase it; the read comes before any headman pass.

dump.label: Dump and chase
dump.desc: Hard rim into the near corner from between the red line and the blue line when a defender is standing up at the line; it wraps behind the net to the far corner, where the weak-side forward is sprinting to beat the defense to it.

cycle.label: Cycle low
cycle.desc: Forwards work the strong-side wall and net front; D at the points. Mirrors to the puck side. The three forwards rotate corner, half wall and net front every few seconds so the cycle keeps moving.

umbrella.label: Umbrella
umbrella.desc: Three up top (point and half walls), two low.

crash.label: Crash the net
crash.desc: Forwards to the slot and crease, point shots through traffic.

motion.desc: Off-puck motion in the offensive zone: how often the cycle spots rotate between the three forwards, and the size of the drift everyone makes around his spot so nobody stands still.

131.desc: One at the point, three across the middle (half walls and the bumper in the slot), one at the net. Built for one-timers from the flanks and the bumper.

umbrella.label: Umbrella
umbrella.desc: Three up top in an arc (point and two half walls), two low at the net and the goal line. Built for point and half-wall shots through traffic.

overload.label: Overload
overload.desc: Four players on the puck side of the ice, one weak-side man. Short passes along the wall to pull the kill out of shape; mirrors to the puck side.

122.label: 1-2-2 (balanced)
122.desc: F1 pressures the puck, two wingers at the tops of the circles ready to jump a pass up the wall, D just inside the far blue line.

212.label: 2-1-2 (aggressive)
212.desc: Two forwards pressure, one high, D at the blue line.

131.label: 1-3-1 trap
131.desc: One forward pressures, three across the neutral zone, one D back.

lwl.label: Left wing lock
lwl.desc: Two forwards forecheck; the left wing locks back with the D to form three across.

neutralDefenseNote: neutral spots are relative to the puck's fx (negative = behind the puck toward our net)

zone.label: Zone (box + 1)
zone.desc: Nearest skater pressures; D hold the top of the crease inside the posts and box out whoever is parked in front; the center owns the slot; wingers shade the point men and half-wall shooters. Any attacker who gets into the slot is picked up by the nearest free defender before anything else.

slotCoverage.desc: The slot is protected first. Every attacker without the puck inside maxFx of our goal line and within halfWidthFt of the middle gets the nearest defender who is not pressuring the carrier or fronting the shot, closest threat first, and that defender plays goalSideFt toward our net and insideFt toward the middle of him. The defender who has a man keeps him unless another free defender is closer by more than stickFt.

dSpread.desc: How far from the middle of the ice each defenseman stands at the net when he has nobody to box out: the strong-side D (the puck's side) at strongSideFt, the weak-side D at weakSideFt. Before sim 0.35 these were 9.5 and 5.5 ft, which left a lane between them at the top of the crease.

man.label: Man-on-man
man.desc: D take the opposing forwards low, forwards take the points and any extra forward. Each defender plays between his man and the net, cushionPerFt of the man's distance from the net (between minCushionFt and maxCushionFt), so he is tight at the crease and already in the way when a man cuts in from the wall. He stays with his man: he switches only when another attacker is closer by more than stickFt, and only the man on the puck carrier pressures him.

box.label: Passive box
box.desc: A tight box in the slot. Nobody chases the puck above the circles; block lanes and keep the middle closed.

diamond.label: Diamond
diamond.desc: One high, two wide, one low. Takes away the point and the half walls against a 1-3-1 or umbrella; the bumper in the slot is the risk.

pressure.label: Aggressive box
pressure.desc: A box that pressures: the nearest killer attacks the puck carrier, clears at the first sign of pressure, and the box collapses behind him.

deployment.desc: Rotation patterns index the line/pair templates; the share of entries is the share of ice time. Shift targets are seconds on ice before the unit looks for a change.

lateCloseGame.desc: 3rd period, under 10 minutes, tied or trailing: shorten the bench

rules: Visitors change first at a stoppage; home team gets the last change and may match lines.
The team that iced the puck may not change.
On the fly: change when our carrier is through the neutral zone (dump it in, or the puck is already deep), or when they are retrieving a puck deep in their own end.
Never change off a loose puck, during a rush against, or while the other team has possession in our zone. A unit stuck defending plays tired instead.
Units stagger: forwards first, defense on the next safe window.
A tired skater near the gate changes alone when play is at the far end and we are not defending.

changeWindows.desc: When a change on the fly is allowed. Own carrier in the neutral zone between the fx bounds (he can dump it in or has crossed the far blue line), or the opponent is retrieving a puck deep in his own end and is not yet moving it up. Loose pucks and any possession in our defensive zone are never a change window; tired units stay out and play tired. A unit with anyone past desperateAfterSec takes the first half-decent window instead: our puck past our own blue line, or a loose puck in their end.

clearing.desc: Under pressure in the defensive zone with no safe pass, a skater bangs the puck off the boards up the near wall; on the penalty kill he clears at the first sign of pressure (icing is waived while shorthanded). A clear that nobody touches before the far end-zone dots is judged for hybrid icing. A gassed unit (anyone past the desperate shift length) clears earlier too, so it can change.

aggression.desc: How hard the team plays on and with the puck. Higher: checkers go after the carrier harder (more takeaways, more penalties), skaters shoot more from ordinary spots, and the carrier holds the puck a beat longer looking for a play. It does not change the forecheck, gap control or line changes; those come from the systems.
